title: CloudHire: Serverless Job Board Platform (Next.js + AWS)
description: 🚀 100% Event-driven Serverless Architecture on AWS, optimizing operational costs to near $0 (NoOps) and auto-scaling with traffic.
⚡️ High Performance: API Gateway & Lambda handling thousands of requests/second, DynamoDB database with millisecond latency.
🛡️ Zero Trust Security: Cognito authentication, IAM Least Privilege authorization, and static content protection with CloudFront OAC.

content.title: Project Information
content.description: Author: Trí Nguyen (Front-end Developer & Cloud Aspirant)
list: Tech Stack: Next.js, AWS Serverless (Lambda, DynamoDB, Cognito, S3, SES, CloudFront)
Target Certification: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03)

content.title: 1. Project Overview
content.description: CloudHire is a high-performance online recruitment platform built entirely on AWS Serverless (Cloud-Native) architecture. The project is designed to solve recruitment system operations with optimal costs, automatic scalability, and high security. This project is an intensive hands-on lab to apply core services commonly found in the AWS SAA-C03 exam, transforming theoretical knowledge into practical experience.
list: Zero Server Management: Completely eliminate server management (No EC2).
Security First: Apply multi-layer security model (Cognito, IAM Least Privilege, OAC).
Cost Optimization: Operational costs near $0 when there's no traffic.
Global Scale: Optimize global access through CDN.

content.title: 2. Business Problem & Solution
content.description: 🔴 The Pain Points: Traditional recruitment systems often face high fixed infrastructure costs, scaling difficulties, operational burden, and poor file security.
list: High fixed infrastructure costs: Must maintain servers 24/7 even with low traffic at night.
Scaling difficulties: System bottlenecks when large numbers of candidates apply simultaneously.
Operational burden: Requires staff to patch OS, manage database, handle backups.
Poor file security: Candidate CVs are easily exposed without strict permissions.

content.title: 🟢 CloudHire Solution (The Serverless Approach)
content.description: CloudHire solves this by using fully managed services from AWS:
list: Authentication: Delegate user management to Amazon Cognito.
Backend: Use AWS Lambda and API Gateway to pay only when there are requests.
Storage: Store CVs on Amazon S3 with 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability.
Database: Use DynamoDB to ensure millisecond latency at any scale.

content.title: 3. System Architecture
content.description: Description of actual deployed data flow:
list: Frontend: Users access Web App (Next.js) hosted on AWS Amplify.
Auth: Users log in via Amazon Cognito (User Pool) to get JWT Token.
API Requests: Client sends request with Token to Amazon API Gateway.
Security Layer: API Gateway uses Cognito Authorizer to authenticate Token.
Compute: API Gateway triggers AWS Lambda (Node.js) to process logic.
Database: Lambda reads/writes recruitment data to Amazon DynamoDB.
File Upload (Direct): Client uploads CV directly to Amazon S3 via Amplify Storage (reduces Lambda load).
File Delivery: Admin views CVs through Amazon CloudFront (configured with OAC to secure S3).
Notifications: Lambda calls Amazon SES to send confirmation email to candidates.
Monitoring: Lambda error -> CloudWatch -> SNS -> Email alert to Admin.

content.title: 3.2. Users & Roles
list: Guest: View job listings (Public API).
Candidate (User): Register/Login, Upload CV, Apply (Authenticated API).
Admin: Manage job posts (CRUD Jobs), View candidate CVs.

content.title: 4. Key Implementation Details
list: Framework: Next.js (React).
Library: AWS Amplify Gen 2 (Auth, Storage).
Hosting: AWS Amplify Hosting (Automatic CI/CD from Git).

content.title: 4.2. Backend & API (Microservices Pattern)
content.description: API system is divided into smaller parts for easier maintenance:
list: GET /jobs: Lambda retrieves job listings (Public).
POST /jobs: Lambda creates new job (Admin only).
POST /apply: Lambda processes application + Sends SES email (Authenticated).
Logic: Validate input -> Check duplicate application -> Save to DynamoDB -> Trigger SES Email.

content.title: 4.3. Database Design (DynamoDB)
content.description: Using NoSQL model with On-demand Capacity:
list: Table Name: DynamoDBCloudJobs.
Partition Key: id (Job ID or Application ID).
Attributes: title, description, cvFileKey, cvUrl, userEmail, status.

content.title: 4.4. Storage & Content Delivery (S3 + CloudFront)
list: Upload: Use Amplify Storage with Cognito Identity Pool to upload directly from browser (Bypass server limitations).
Security: S3 Bucket blocks all Public Access.
Access: Use CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC). Only CloudFront has permission to read files from S3. CV links are served via CloudFront for speed and security.

content.title: 4.5. Monitoring & Alerting (DevOps)
list: Logging: CloudWatch Logs records all Lambda activities.
Alarm: CloudWatch Alarm monitors Errors metric. If Errors >= 1 in 5 minutes -> Triggers SNS Topic.
Notification: SNS sends immediate email alert to Admin for incident handling.

content.title: 5. Cost Estimation
content.description: Assumption: Production system with 1,000 Active Users/month, 3 million API requests.
list: Amplify Hosting: Build minutes + Data transfer ~$3.00
AWS Lambda: 3M requests + Compute time (128MB) ~$8.10
API Gateway: $3.50/1M requests ~$10.50
DynamoDB: On-demand R/W units (Very cheap with text data) ~$1.70
Amazon S3: Storage + Requests (PUT/GET) ~$1.54
CloudFront: Data transfer out (CV download) ~$8.10
Cognito: 50,000 MAU Free Tier (Almost free) $0.00
Amazon SES: 62,000 emails Free Tier (Almost free) $0.00
TOTAL: ~$32.94 / month

content.title: Cost Note
content.description: This cost is much cheaper than renting a traditional EC2 t2.medium ($30) + RDS ($15) + ELB ($18), and requires no maintenance effort.

content.title: 6. AWS SAA-C03 Alignment
content.description: This project directly applies the 4 pillars of AWS Well-Architected Framework:
list: Security: Identity & Access Management (Cognito, IAM Roles), Data Protection (S3 Private, CloudFront OAC), Infrastructure Protection (API Gateway Throttling).
Reliability: Decoupled system between Upload and Logic processing. DynamoDB and S3 have high availability by default.
Performance Efficiency: Serverless (Lambda) auto-scales with traffic. CloudFront caches static content at Edge locations.
Cost Optimization: Pay only when used (Pay-as-you-go). S3 Lifecycle (planned) to delete old CVs after 30 days.

content.title: 7. Future Roadmap
content.description: To upgrade the system to Enterprise level, the following features will be implemented:
list: AWS WAF: Protect API Gateway from SQL Injection and DDoS attacks.
AWS X-Ray: Trace requests to debug latency between services.
DynamoDB Streams: Trigger Lambda for post-processing (e.g., AI CV analysis) when new records are created.
IaC (Terraform/CDK): Convert manual configuration (ClickOps) to Code for automated infrastructure deployment.
